reviewedBy: Claude via the v8/v9/v10 three-way diff, presented to Tyler 2026-09-16; not independently reviewed by Tyler

base.rationale: Pick an EHR that fits our workflows, integrates with billing and payers, keeps us compliant, and protects clinician productivity at a sustainable total cost.

scenarios.label: Enterprise ambulatory rollout
scenarios.description: Health system standardizes owned and affiliated outpatient clinics onto one EHR under central governance, integration, and security requirements.

scenarios.label: Multi-site group replacement
scenarios.description: Independent 20 - 200 provider group replaces a legacy EHR/PM to improve clinician workflows, analytics, interoperability, and denial management.

scenarios.label: Physician-owner pick
scenarios.description: A 1 - 5 provider private practice where the physician-owner makes the call quickly while balancing clinic operations and cost.

scenarios.label: RCM bundle selection
scenarios.description: Practice chooses an EHR tightly bundled with outsourced billing to stabilize collections, reporting, and staffing coverage.

cellTexts: [problem_recognition|Enterprise ambulatory rollout|generic] Rolling out a common setup across 30+ outpatient clinics and everything's fractured: scheduling, charting, refills, referrals. Nothing talks to each other and reporting is a mess. Where do I even start to get this under control for go-live?

[problem_recognition|Multi-site group replacement|generic] We've got 10 clinics on a patchwork of systems, upgrades keep breaking workflows, denials are up, and clinicians are spending nights finishing notes. If we rip this out, how do we do it without blowing up schedules and losing historical data?

[problem_recognition|Physician-owner pick|generic] I'm the physician-owner for a small group. I need something that lets us see patients, finish notes the same day, and get paid without me babysitting tech. Too many clicks, too much after-hours charting, and surprise fees are killing us. What am I actually looking for here?

[problem_recognition|RCM bundle selection|generic] Our outpatient group's revenue ops are all over the place. Eligibility misses, coding edits caught late, claims bouncing back and forth, and no clean view of A/R by location. Front desk, clinical, and billing live in different worlds. How do practices fix this end to end?
[category_education|-|generic] For an outpatient practice, what does an ambulatory EHR actually do, beyond basic charting? Where does it start and stop versus practice management and billing?

[discovery|Enterprise ambulatory rollout|generic] What are the best EHR options for an enterprise rollout across 40+ ambulatory clinics with centralized scheduling, standardized templates, and strong reporting?

[discovery|Multi-site group replacement|generic] Best outpatient EHR for replacing a multi-site group's aging system? Need fast charting, painless data migration, solid RCM tie-in, and minimal downtime.

[discovery|Physician-owner pick|generic] As a physician-owner, what are the best EHRs for a small outpatient group that value clinician workflow, transparent pricing, and responsive support? I care more about reliability than buzzwords.
[discovery|RCM bundle selection|generic] Best integrated EHR + RCM bundle for an ambulatory group that wants eligibility up front, clean claims, tight coding edits, and real-time A/R analytics?
[shortlist|Enterprise ambulatory rollout|generic] Shortlist 3 to 5 EHRs built for an enterprise ambulatory rollout with strong interoperability, role-based controls, and enterprise reporting.
[shortlist|Multi-site group replacement|generic] For a 12-location group replacement, give me 3 or 4 outpatient EHRs worth a demo that handle data conversion well and won't slow clinicians down.
[shortlist|Physician-owner pick|generic] I'm the deciding physician-owner. Give me 3 small-group outpatient EHRs you'd trust for low after-hours charting, fair contracts, and strong support.
[shortlist|RCM bundle selection|generic] Name 3 integrated EHR + RCM bundles to evaluate for an ambulatory group, with front-to-back revenue workflows and built-in analytics.

[criteria|Enterprise ambulatory rollout|generic] Planning an enterprise ambulatory EHR rollout across about 70 clinics tied to our hospital. What should matter most when choosing - interoperability with inpatient, role-based security and SSO, centralized scheduling, analytics at scale, data migration, training and go-live support, uptime SLAs, API openness?

[criteria|Multi-site group replacement|generic] replacing the EHR across 12 locations. what should drive the decision so we don't end up with the same headaches? thinking data conversion quality, template governance, RCM fit, provider adoption, cutover risk, and long-term cost to run.

[criteria|Physician-owner pick|generic] Physician-owner here (9 providers). I need an ambulatory EHR I can live with for 7-10 years. What should I weigh most - proof of reliability, data control and exit terms, transparent pricing, real references I can call, training burden, charting speed? I'm deciding slowly and want reasons, not hype.

[criteria|RCM bundle selection|generic] Considering an ambulatory EHR bundled with RCM services. Beyond the headline percent fee, what should I scrutinize - clean-claim rates, denial prevention and management, coding support, payer connectivity, patient pay workflows, reporting transparency, and who owns the data and money flow?

[use_case|Enterprise ambulatory rollout|generic] Need to stand up centralized scheduling and referral management across 50 clinics, with a pooled call center and specialty-specific rules. In an ambulatory EHR, what's the clean way to model locations, provider pools, templates, and access so we don't tank productivity?

[use_case|Multi-site group replacement|generic] We're swapping out our EHR across 14 sites in a single quarter. How would you structure data migration (problems/meds/allergies, labs, scanned docs), code and phrase mapping, and a weekend cutover so Monday's clinics run without chaos?

[use_case|Physician-owner pick|generic] I run a 7-provider family practice. Day to day I need fast charting, e-prescribe that just works, labs and imaging interfaces, telehealth, and e-fax. Walk me through what our first month could look like on a new ambulatory EHR - training plan, go-live support, and keeping visit times from ballooning.

[use_case|RCM bundle selection|generic] If we go with an EHR + RCM bundle, how would charge capture flow from visit to claim, with eligibility, coding edits, prior auth, and denial workqueues? Also need to handle multiple NPIs, global periods, capitation, and shared services across locations.
[social_validation|-|generic] what are ambulatory admins actually happy with right now? where do folks share candid reviews or benchmarks for EHRs, and any recent neutral reports worth checking?

[comparison|Enterprise ambulatory rollout|Epic] For an enterprise ambulatory rollout across 60+ clinics, compare athenahealth vs Epic. Implementation timeline, integration with a hospital inpatient system, centralized scheduling, governance at scale, reporting, and total 5-year cost to run - where do they differ most?

[comparison|Multi-site group replacement|Cerner] We're replacing an EHR across 18 ambulatory sites. Head to head: athenahealth vs Cerner for multi-site groups - data conversion support, template standardization, provider onboarding, revenue cycle integration, interfaces, and what the first 90 days look like. Any gotchas?

[comparison|Physician-owner pick|eClinicalWorks] I'm the physician-owner of a 10-provider practice. Talk me through athenahealth vs eClinicalWorks as if you were advising a colleague: reliability, charting speed, support you can actually reach, data ownership and exit clauses, reporting for quality, and real total cost. I'm fine with tradeoffs; I just want the logic.

[comparison|RCM bundle selection|NextGen Healthcare] For an ambulatory EHR bundled with RCM, how does athenahealth compare to NextGen Healthcare on clean-claim rates, denial management workflows, coding assistance, patient pay, transparency in fees, and who does what day to day? Include typical contract terms if relevant.

[objections|Enterprise ambulatory rollout|generic] Rolling out to 40 ambulatory sites next year. Be straight with me: does athenahealth bog down at scale? I keep hearing about slow chart loads 8 to 10 am. Any real numbers on uptime and typical page load with 500+ concurrent users?

[objections|Multi-site group replacement|generic] Replacing our EHR across 12 clinics. My worry with athenahealth is performance when everyone hits scheduling, eRx, and orders at the same time. Do you have client-facing SLAs or benchmarks so I know click-to-save isn't 3 to 4 seconds at peak?

[objections|Physician-owner pick|generic] I'm a physician-owner, 3 providers. I like a lot about athenahealth, but I will not live with lag in the exam room. On standard laptops and decent cable internet, what are real-world load times for chart open, order entry, note save? Uptime history too, please.

[objections|RCM bundle selection|generic] Looking at athenahealth EHR bundled with their RCM. How does performance hold under end-of-month spikes for charge capture, claim scrubbing, and posting? Any turnaround or processing time guarantees so we don't see queues pile up?

[pricing|Enterprise ambulatory rollout|generic] i need a budget for an enterprise ambulatory rollout, about 120 providers across 40 sites. what's a realistic per-provider monthly for an ambulatory EHR at that scale, plus interfaces and data conversion? is any free option actually viable or does it cost us elsewhere?

[pricing|Multi-site group replacement|generic] For a 12-site group moving this year, what does athenahealth typically cost all-in? Per-provider fee or percent of collections, and what extras hit the bill like interfaces, eRx, texting, training? I need a clean number for finance.

[pricing|Physician-owner pick|generic] physician-owner here trying to make a rational call. for a 3 doc practice, what's the 5 year total cost of an ambulatory EHR including setup, interfaces, support, and the productivity dip during go-live? is going with a free system a false economy?

[pricing|RCM bundle selection|generic] If we take athenahealth with RCM, how is pricing structured? Percent of collections, minimums, and what's included vs add-on fees like eligibility, statements, and credentialing. Does the EHR subscription get discounted in the bundle?

[business_case|Enterprise ambulatory rollout|generic] I've got to make the case to our CFO for athenahealth on an enterprise ambulatory rollout. Can you help me frame ROI with concrete numbers we can defend, like days in A/R improvement, denial rates, provider throughput, and IT cost offsets?

[business_case|Multi-site group replacement|generic] We're replacing a patchwork EHR across 12 clinics. I need a board-ready rationale for athenahealth that balances migration cost against gains in standard workflows, reporting, compliance, and ongoing support. Help me put that into CFO language.

[business_case|RCM bundle selection|generic] Need to justify athenahealth's EHR + RCM to our CFO. How do I translate the take rate into net collections lift versus in-house billing, expected FTE changes, denial prevention impact, and cash flow timing? Also what KPIs should we bake into the contract?

[churn_triggers|-|generic] Current athenahealth customer, 5 years. Lately feeling slower screens, more support tickets, and price creep. How do I tell if we should stick it out and tune things vs start planning a move? What checkpoints would you run before deciding?

[alternatives|-|defensive] If we moved off athenahealth for ambulatory, what EHRs should a 12-provider multi-specialty group actually shortlist? Key needs are clean scheduling, solid RCM, patient portal that patients will use.
[alternatives|-|Epic] Not going with Epic. For a 10-provider outpatient group, what ambulatory EHRs are legit alternatives that won't take a year to implement?
[alternatives|-|Cerner] We want out of Cerner for our outpatient clinics. What ambulatory EHRs would fit a mid-size multi-site group, especially strong on claims and operational reporting?
[alternatives|-|eClinicalWorks] eClinicalWorks isn't landing well with our docs. What other ambulatory EHRs should we look at that have fast charting and clean eRx?

[alternatives|-|NextGen Healthcare] NextGen Healthcare feels heavy for our 8-provider primary care. Which lighter ambulatory EHRs are worth a trial that can still handle referrals and prior auth smoothly?

[renewal|-|generic] Our athenahealth renewal is up this summer. For a 14-provider ambulatory group, is it worth staying or are there clearly cheaper EHR options that won't wreck our RCM? How would you structure the eval before I sign?

[problem_resolution|-|generic] athenahealth claims are stuck in Ready to Submit after clearinghouse enrollment warnings from a payer change. How do I clear or bulk re-enroll so we can push everything out today without opening 20 tickets?

[expansion|-|generic] We're happy on athenahealth at two family med sites. Thinking about rolling it out to our urgent care and adding telehealth and online check-in. Anything to watch for with licensing, scheduling templates, or patient flow?

[ecosystem|-|generic] On athenahealth, what add-ons play nicely for patient texting and reminders, digital intake, and centralized scheduling? Looking for options that sync insurance and appointment types without a bunch of custom interfaces.

[advocacy|-|generic] I need to defend athenahealth to a skeptical physician board. What metrics or proof points matter most for ambulatory practices, and how do I preempt the usual complaints from clinicians and billing?
